input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 (the first clause bearing that number) imposes an MFN running against us: before engaging any other provider we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive. It is not limited to a defined product, has no 12-month sunset, and contains no like-for-like comparison carve-outs, so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory (open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor). It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. We therefore return to the preferred position by removing the disclose-and-match obligation, leaving the rest of the fee provisions untouched.

proposal.summary: Remove the Customer-side obligation to disclose and match more favourable third-party offers.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the open-ended obligation for us to disclose and match any more favourable offer we receive, since our playbook does not accept an MFN running in Vendor's favour and this conflicts with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

ops.oldText: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: Customer has no obligation to disclose or match for Vendor any commercial offer it receives from another provider.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
